note: Roof viewing terrace of the Rotunda complex on Chopok as in the 2016 photos (wooden deck, glass railing on a solid dark parapet), looking north-east: the Liptov basin and the High Tatras over the railing, the Funitel line going down on the left, the rocky Chopok peak rising on the right with the Atlas pavilion's roof seen below through the glass. Camera ~2.1 m high on the deck; horizon y ~380; the parapet stands on the deck's back edge at y ~720 (~161 px per metre there: parapet top y ~623, handrail y ~543). Perspective s(y) = (y - 380) / 635. Left: the top of the external steel stairs down to the plateau (exit); right: the separately labelled low-voltage Atlas cabinet with the mechanical ZAPIS/MONITOR switch and, on its own post beside it, the separate return connector with the ceramic bridge. The third-party dragon sculpture of the photos is left out. The walk polygon leaves out the cabinet's base (foot y ~740).
